quote: man wird wahrscheinlich semiconvergente Reihen erhalten
english: one will probably obtain semiconvergent series
topic: The page discusses how hard it is to prove that a differential equation cannot be solved by a single quadrature, then asks how solids, liquids, gases, aether and electricity should be described under molecular theory using mean values and expansions in small parameters, and finally states that the function zeta(s,x) = sum x^n/n^s satisfies no known differential equation.

triage.modern_statement: If you derive macroscopic continuum equations (for solids, liquids, gases, the aether, electricity) from a molecular model by averaging and expanding in a small parameter (for example the mean free path or Knudsen number), the series you get will probably be semiconvergent: asymptotic but generally divergent rather than convergent. The modern version of this is the question of whether the Hilbert and Chapman-Enskog expansions of the Boltzmann equation converge or are only asymptotic, which is part of Hilbert's 6th problem programme (going from kinetic theory to continuum mechanics).
triage.answered_by: Partly confirmed later. Hilbert himself introduced the Hilbert expansion for the Boltzmann equation (1912). Chapman and Enskog developed their expansion (around 1916-17). Grad showed that the Chapman-Enskog expansion, even if divergent, is asymptotic to a class of Boltzmann solutions. Caflisch (CPAM 33, 1980) used a truncated Hilbert expansion to justify the fluid limit rigorously. Divergence of the Chapman-Enskog expansion is now standard knowledge. Deng, Hani and Ma (2025, arXiv 2503.01800) derived the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations from Newtonian hard-sphere dynamics via Boltzmann's kinetic theory. The 6th problem in its full generality is still considered open.

evidence.claim: Grad showed the Chapman-Enskog expansion, even if divergent, is asymptotic to a class of solutions of the Boltzmann equation
The Chapman-Enskog expansion is an asymptotic, and generally divergent, solution of the Boltzmann equation
Caflisch 1980 (CPAM 33:651-666) began the use of the Hilbert expansion to rigorously justify fluid limits of the Boltzmann equation
Deng, Hani and Ma rigorously derived the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations from Newtonian particle dynamics via Boltzmann's kinetic theory (Hilbert's 6th problem)
One critique argues that the 6th problem remains open in its full generality

triage.why: The remark is a heuristic prediction inside Hilbert's programme of deriving continuum physics from molecular theory, which later became the 6th problem. Expansions in small parameters such as the Hilbert and Chapman-Enskog expansions turned out to be generally divergent but asymptotic, which fits 'semiconvergent'. The note is vague: it does not say which expansion or which physical system, so this match is an interpretation rather than a confirmed identification. Rigorous derivation of hydrodynamic limits is still very active (Deng-Hani-Ma 2025 and follow-up work).
